instruction: Pick up the blue block with the left arm, hand it over to the right arm in the air, and let the right arm put it in the green square; then both arms let go and move away.

outcome.real_measurement: Block centre inside the right target square at every judged step: min(half - |dx|, half - |dy|) >= 0. Real world: top camera, block centre vs the marked square.
Resting on the table: lowest block corner within 5 mm of the table top at every judged step. Real world: RGB-D pose vs the table plane.

The handover happened in the air: at some point the block was carried by the left arm alone (airborne: no table contact, bottom > 3 mm above the table; only the left robot in contact) for >= 5 control steps (0.25 s), later by the right arm alone for >= 5 steps, and it did not touch the table in between. Derived from per-step contact signals by imsim.verify.handover.handover_signal (signals armL_obj_impulse_Ns, armR_obj_impulse_Ns, table_obj_impulse_Ns, obj_bottom_dz_m). Real world: wrist F/T or gripper current per arm + side camera for table contact.

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of the block retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; the block must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the obj centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

counterexamples.name: handover
counterexamples.description: positive control: left picks, mid-air handover, right places, both open and retreat

counterexamples.name: no_handover
counterexamples.description: the right arm reaches over and picks the block from the left zone itself, places it in the target, opens and retreats; the left arm never moves

counterexamples.name: both_hold
counterexamples.description: handover grasp by the right arm while the left keeps holding; both arms carry the block towards the target (the largest fraction both can reach) and set it down on the table, neither opens

counterexamples.name: drop_and_push
counterexamples.description: the left arm lifts the block and drops it near the centre; the right arm pushes it along the table into the target, both grippers open at the end

counterexamples.name: table_transfer
counterexamples.description: the left arm puts the block down on the table near the centre, opens and leaves; the right arm picks it up from the table, places it in the target, opens and retreats (no mid-air handover)

source.protocol: v3 (veritask/adapters/protocol_v3.py, unchanged) + imsim v3.2 signals (imsim/imsim/verify/v32.py): position-based speeds, all-link enclosure, retreat aftermath, commanded vs actual opening, 5 s settle cap
source.released_code_predicate: block centre in the target square, block bottom within 5 mm of the table, PhysX speed < 2 cm/s, both grippers measured open >= 80 % of their maximum, at the policy's last step (RoboTwin handover_block style; no handover check)

notes: v2 = v1 + the E24c fixes (v3.2). End-state terms 1-2 and the at-rest terms are v1's thresholds on the v3.2 signals (objs_speed = fastest bounding-box corner speed from positions; v1 used PhysX's reported block velocity), the handover term and the retreat aftermath are v1's, release = robot contact (all links of both robots, substep-accumulated) + all-link enclosure 2 mm as v1, new: commanded-vs-actual opening term and settle cap 5 s (v1: 3 s).
